channel.title: Brandon Leon
channel.description: Essays and research notes on public markets.

item.title: The Next Guide Sets the Grade
item.description: Nvidia reports after the close. We're publishing our pass/fail test before the release — the next-quarter guide vs. $100B and $95B — so it can be graded in public either way. Plus the $105B OpenAI lease guarantee and our first Nvidia disclosure.

item.title: The Hawks Were Counted
item.description: The Fed minutes showed broader rate-hike sympathy than the 9–3 vote implied. Retail earnings split the consumer story — and Walmart decides whether that's category mix or broader demand. One week before Warsh's first Jackson Hole speech.

item.title: Soft Data, Hard Prices — Week of August 17
item.description: Jobs, inflation, retail spending, and sentiment all weakened. Long yields, oil, and near-term inflation expectations did not. Five wires graded, the open gate still unbought, and the retailers cross-examine the retail print. Charts inside.

item.title: The Gates Opened — Deployment Series No. 2
item.description: The CPI branch fired cool, the 30-year cleared at 2001 prices, the gates re-armed — and the authorized buy went untaken. The honest accounting, the duration stance retiring on schedule, and the repair. Charts inside.

item.title: Week Ahead — August 10, 2026
item.description: Nine days after three Fed dissents FOR a hike, July payrolls printed negative. The story of the week the regime cracked — the gates we didn't walk through, AMD's lesson about price, and the two endings already written for Wednesday's CPI. Five charts.

item.title: The Most Valuable Company in China Makes the Cheapest Chips in the World
item.description: CXMT displaced ICBC in one trading day and knocked a trillion dollars off global chip stocks. We hold memory. So we underwrote the fear properly: what China's champion actually makes, what it can't make yet, and the two tripwires that would change our mind.

item.title: Week Ahead — August 3, 2026
item.description: A 9-3 hawkish hold, the 30-year's first close above 5.2% since 2007, a capex week that paid Microsoft and punished everyone else — and the Micron exit that finally executed itself: ~+53% blended, twelve weeks, ledger closed. The wires reset for jobs, the minutes, and the war-oil CPI.

item.title: Where the Next Dollar Goes — Deployment Series No. 1
item.description: The exit funded a question. This note opens the deployment series: the hurdle (cash yields 4% and the equity cushion is roughly zero), the framework (correlation budget + the self-funded-capex axis), five lanes surveyed honestly, and the dated gates that decide when money moves.

item.title: Micron broke $900 again. This time the order was already there.
item.description: CXMT debuted +466%, the complex shed $1T, Micron touched $705 — and the broker stop placed after the confession had already sold the runner at ~$900. The call closes at ~+53%: the exact floor the system promised. Final ledger inside.

item.title: Micron closed below $900. Our rule said sell. We didn’t.
item.description: The stop fired July 16. We didn't sell — and today Micron ripped 12.2%. The violation is ahead of the rule tonight. Ahead is not the same as right: the process failure, graded in public, with the tighter line that replaces it.

item.title: Week Ahead — July 20, 2026
item.description: The graded ledger: a cool CPI the note pre-answered, a toolmaker paid and a spender punished, memory in a bear market — and the $900 Micron rule that fired without being followed. The violation is graded F in the stop note. Now the capex gate opens: Alphabet Wednesday.

item.title: ASML — Initiation. Paid by Both Sides of the Memory War.
item.description: We waited for the air-pocket, bought the crash at $1,752.87, and this morning's Q2 print proved it: a beat above the top of guidance and the third full-year raise in six months, to 43-45 billion euros. Initiating at ACCUMULATE, PW target ~$2,000. Add-zone $1,550-1,650 — do not chase.

item.title: Micron round-tripped again. KeyBanc raised its target to $1,750. We didn’t.
item.description: A $55 whipsaw on no news, a fresh $1,750 KeyBanc upgrade, and our ~$1,100 target — the low end of a range that tops out at $2,000, level with Goldman's Neutral. The argument isn't demand; it's what Micron keeps. ASML settles it tomorrow.

item.title: Week Ahead — July 13, 2026
item.description: The Warsh minutes floated a June hike, yields broke our levels while the auctions stopped through, the Iran ceasefire collapsed, and Micron pierced $900 intraday but never on a close — then SK hynix raised $26.5B and memory rallied. The graded ledger, and the loaded week: CPI, five banks, and Warsh's debut testimony in one morning.

item.title: Samsung posted the biggest profit in the world. Memory made new lows. That’s the tell.
item.description: A world-record $58.4B profit couldn't lift memory — Micron made a new low while Nvidia rose. We cut the target to ~$1,100 and explain why we bought the basket, not more Micron.

item.title: The bounce came with names attached. Micron’s was the smallest. Friday is why.
item.description: UBS +32% Q3 DRAM, BofA's healthy reset at $1,550, Citi's upside watch, Samsung's record print due Tuesday — and Micron still bounced least. The SKHY debut Friday is the test, and we initiated ASML.

item.title: Week Ahead — July 6, 2026
item.description: A soft, strange jobs print took the September hike off the table. Meta's excess-compute move cratered memory — for now — while the spenders rallied. The honest grades, the unwind, and the week of the first Warsh minutes and the SK hynix debut.

item.title: Micron round-tripped the best quarter in its history. What the unwind is — and isn’t.
item.description: Two days, −15.5%, and the whole blowout pop is gone. The unwind was memory-shaped, not market-shaped. The catalysts, the collar the market ignored, the honest re-rate, and the $900 line.

item.title: Week Ahead — June 29, 2026
item.description: MU printed a record $41.5B with a $50B next-quarter guide and $100B of contracted demand. It ripped while megacap tech sagged on AI costs. The supplier-vs-spender split, the jobs print Thursday under a hawkish Fed, and a first look at quantum.

item.title: Micron didn’t fade. It ripped 16%. What we got wrong — and the contract that rewrote the thesis.
item.description: We said priced-and-likely-to-fade. It ripped 16% to a record. What we got wrong, why the scale-out still won, and the SCA collar that re-rates the thesis from $1,100 toward $1,500.

item.title: Everyone Agrees on Micron Now. Tomorrow It Has to Print.
item.description: MU set a record high the day before its biggest print and the whole sell-side finally caught up. The bar moved with the price. The in-quarter beat is priced; the FQ4 guide and HBM4 ASPs decide the tape. PT stays $1,100; the $1,100 trim trigger hit June 18.

item.title: Week Recap — June 19, 2026
item.description: The hawkish-hold call died on the 2-year (+16bp, biggest Fed-day jump since 2008). Dots flipped to a 2026 hike. We own the miss. Then equities shrugged it off by Thursday. The week, graded.

item.title: SpaceX — Initiation. A World-Class Moat, Priced for a Flawless 2030.
item.description: Largest IPO ever; ~111x sales; losing $4.9B a year. Initiating at HOLD, fair value ~$115, target $135. The melt-up we refused to chase has already round-tripped 26%. Starlink earns it, xAI burns it.

item.title: Week Ahead — June 16, 2026
item.description: A three-year-high CPI got overrun by an Iran peace deal that collapsed oil to the low $80s. S&P rallied to ~7,550, 10Y fell to ~4.4%. Wednesday, the new Fed Chair debuts with a hawkish hold the market has already priced. The pain trade is up.

item.title: Dell — Initiation. Start With What We Got Wrong.
item.description: The re-rate ran 9× to 24× before the earnings did the work. Initiating at HOLD, accumulation ladder $320 / $285 / $250, PW reference ~$340. The Street's $484 average PT is our bull case.
